title: Spatial Involvement
role_in_volume: DIMENSION CHAPTER (1 of 6). Operationalizes the spatial dimension of the Player Involvement Model. Macro phase = Exploration (off-line affective draw of unfamiliar lands + on-line drive toward unmapped regions); micro phase = Navigating Space, subsuming a five-fold taxonomy of spatial structures (unicursal corridors, multicursal mazes, rhizomatic zones, open landscapes, arenas) plus a passage from Space to Place (Tuan-anchored internalization) and the Space of Miniatures (disembodied isometric/RTS spatiality). The chapter is the dissertation's premier Layer-C anchor site: every move Calleja makes in phenomenological register (orientation, getting-lost, habitation, internalization, vista, comfort/belonging) is grounded NOT in canonical phenomenology but in humanistic geography (Tuan), urban perception (Lynch), and behavioral psychology (Tolman). Per Phase 0 critical finding confirmed by full-text scan, Calleja cites NO Uexküll, NO Gibson, NO Merleau-Ponty, NO Heidegger in this chapter. All Layer-C edges (Umwelt, Verlorenheit, phantasia spatial-imagery, Burke Scene) therefore carry provenance='anticipatory-projection (dissertation)'. The Umwelt ↔ virtual-environment-habitation mapping is the signature Layer-C payoff: Uexküll's biosemiotic Umwelt is arguably MORE apt than Heideggerian In-der-Welt-sein for designer-constituted bounded environments — and Calleja's Tuan/Lynch/Tolman scaffolding supplies precisely the cognitive-cartographic + imageability + body-relative-orientation machinery onto which the Umwelt + Merkwelt+Wirkwelt apparatus maps without strain.

phase2_pass_log.pass_3_complete: Layer-A residual-phenomenology anchor catalog + anticipatory Umwelt mapping with rationale

dimension_operational_definition: Spatial involvement is the player's habitation-oriented engagement with the simulated, navigable space of a virtual environment, comprising (a) macro-phase exploration drive and (b) micro-phase navigation-plus-cognitive-mapping that internalizes the environment across nested scales — immediate / map / level / region / world — and converts perceived space into experienced place.
boundary_criteria: (B1) Concerns SIMULATED, navigable space (Wolf 2009) — not merely represented space in non-ergodic media (literature, film). Player must move and act within it.

(B2) Mapping internalizes the environment across NESTED SCALES (immediate / map / level / region / world). Single-scale attention to immediate surroundings without scale-stitching is partial spatial involvement only.

(B3) Distinguished from KINESTHETIC by orientation toward LOCATION-IN-ENVIRONMENT rather than control-of-avatar-movement; the two are interdependent (cornerstone-pair, see IG-10) but conceptually severable — spatial is about WHERE, kinesthetic is about HOW-TO-MOVE.

(B4) Distinguished from SHARED by absence-or-marginality of co-player cohabitation as the engagement vector; spatial can saturate solo-player experience (single-player open-landscape RPGs) whereas shared requires co-presence.

(B5) Encompasses both AVATAR-EMBODIED spatiality (1st/3rd person) and MINIATURE/DISEMBODIED spatiality (isometric RTS, board-game derivatives); the latter exhibits tactical-control spatial involvement without systemically upheld habitation (cannot be lost).

(B6) Includes the AESTHETIC-AFFECTIVE pull of landscape (the 'tourist moment') as part of the macro phase, not a separate affective concern; spatial macro carries its own affective tonality that the dimension model does not export to IG-08.

outline.title: Macro Phase: Exploration
outline.summary: Calleja opens by anchoring exploration as a species-level disposition (Lewis-Williams 1998/2002; Evans 2001) and immediately routes it through Tuan 1998 on the urbanization-driven romanticization of pastoral/exotic landscape. Digital games and virtual worlds appease the exploration penchant by simulating traversable, picturesque expanses that exceed what non-ergodic visual media can offer: literature can prompt mental imagery of represented space, but ergodic environments demand that players navigate, not merely imagine. The 'tourist moment' (Rheric, WoW) and 'pretty/exotic-holiday' testimony (Baal, WoW) are introduced as paradigm exploration-affect data. The macro phase closes by introducing the avatar's body-relative orientation (front/back/left/right, with futurity-ahead) via Tuan 2007 — a phenomenology of bodily orientation that Calleja treats as transferable from physical to virtual environments. The achievement-of-distant-destination quote (Ananke, WoW) anchors the affective-effort dimension.

outline.title: Lost in the Game World
outline.summary: The sub-section that does the chapter's heaviest phenomenological work, paradoxically without ANY phenomenological citation. Getting-lost is reframed as a productive condition for spatial involvement: it requires spatial contingency, which requires that the environment extend beyond what is immediately perceptible — Klastrup 2004's 'worldness.' Once players realize there is no opportunity to become lost, the environment collapses into a multicursal labyrinth and the scope for exploration is diminished. The Aarseth 2005 anchor (labyrinthine spatial structures very common in games; once unraveled they collapse to linear progressions). The pivotal Tuan 2007 lost-in-forest passage is quoted at length (lines 2589-2599): bodily-orientation regions (front/back/right/left) remain organized in conformity with the body but lose external reference; a flickering light establishes a goal and front-back recover meaning. Calleja transfers this directly to virtual environments: goal-directed movement (quest, NPC-set, player-set) reinforces avatar tangibility by giving it meaningful directional structure. Borges 1972 'labyrinth devised by men, destined to be deciphered by men' is invoked as literary figure for the designer-constituted character of game worlds. Malaby 2007 grounds the appeal of game-worlds in their representation of CONTINGENCY: maze-traversal promises a solution (contrived contingency), uncharted bush does not (real contingency); game-design fabricates 'complex, implicit, contingent conditions wherein the texture of engaged human experience can happen.'

outline.title: Micro Phase: Navigating Space
outline.summary: Pivot to micro phase. Three forms of spatial engagement: (i) learning the environment through navigation, (ii) mentally mapping the navigated space, (iii) controlling miniature space through tactical interventions. Before treating these, Calleja imports Mark Wolf 2009's definition of 'navigable space': interconnected spatial cells through which the avatar moves, network often organized like a maze, much of the space off-screen, accessibility relying on player's navigational ability. Navigable space is necessarily SIMULATED, not merely represented.

outline.title: Spatial Structures: Unicursal Corridors or Labyrinths
outline.summary: Paradigm: Medal of Honor: Allied Assault (2002) opening (Figure 5.1). The Saving-Private-Ryan-resembling beach landing scene appears expansive but contains a single traversable path; cliff barriers, artillery, and chaos disguise the unicursal structure. After repeated death along the western flank, players form an updated cognitive map of the invisible-wall barrier. Tolman 1948 cognitive-mapping citation introduced and operationalized via Golledge+Garling 2004 ('encoding, storing, manipulating experienced and sensed information that can be spatially referenced'). Liboriussen 2009: cognitive map as a mental tool aiding virtual-world navigation AND providing sense of how the virtual world is structured + sense of connectedness. Aarseth 2005 'unicursal corridors' label imported. Nitsche 2008 distinguishes labyrinths from 'tracks and rails' (the racing-game variant; Gran Turismo 1998) — Calleja COLLAPSES this distinction because his taxonomy is based on traversable rather than visible space. Fernandez-Vara 2007 on classical labyrinths offering no test — Calleja qualifies: game labyrinths always contain adversity (puzzles, enemies). Half-Life 2 (2004) example combines both forms of barrier in alternation. King+Krzywinska 2006: spatial restriction enables tighter designer control of other involvement dimensions (especially scripted narrative in Ch.7 and orchestrated affect in Ch.8).

outline.title: Spatial Structures: Multicursal Corridors or Mazes
outline.summary: Branching paths and dead ends; encourage navigational attention and mental mapping (Fernandez-Vara 2007). Mental mapping is necessary only when the maze is presented in 1st/3rd-person and extends beyond the individual screen — Fable (2004) is the in-perspective paradigm; players are channeled through pathways formed by steep hills and rock formations, with desert + heat exhaustion forming the outer ring barrier. Compared with omniscient-perspective games like Pacman (1980): the latter's spatial learning is more akin to indexing a Google Map than to navigation-based mental cartography. The location-anchoring of perspective is the major differentiator.

outline.title: Spatial Structures: Rhizomatic Zones
outline.summary: Non-contiguous game spaces linked by teleportation. Fable II (2008): predefined teleport points within already-discovered areas. Mass Effect (2007): separate zones reachable only via teleport entry points. Deleuze+Guattari 1987's rhizome (linked points, no hierarchy or center, multiplicity with no beginning/center/end, multiple entry points, non-linear, resilient to local damage) is imported as the conceptual frame. Even when contiguous, game spaces contain breaks-in-navigational-flow as new zones load; designers conceal these by diegetic transit — Dead Space (2008) elevator journeys allow inventory/weapon management during the load.

outline.title: Spatial Structures: Open Landscapes
outline.summary: Maximum navigational freedom. The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion (2006) as paradigm RPG; MMOGs (Lord of the Rings Online 2007) similarly large. Travel restrictions tend to be RULE-based (mob difficulty) rather than SPATIAL-structural (the LotRO Hobbit-to-Rivendell example). Babic 2007 introduces the absolute-vs-relational space distinction (via Martina Löw 2001): absolute = Euclidean container, objectively-measurable arrangements; relational = constituted by relations and interactions of actors and objects within it. Lefebvre 1991, Soja 1996, Tuan 1974 cluster as the relational-space theorists. Babic associates pre-MMOG game-space with absolute-perspective design, MMOGs with relational-space transformation through persistent social interaction. Calleja frames Babic's argument in PIM terms: MMOG spatial dimension overlaps intimately with shared dimension; Doom (1993) spatial dimension overlaps with kinesthetic.

outline.title: Spatial Structures: Arenas
outline.summary: Nitsche 2008: arenas provide 'the canvas for a performance' rather than navigational cues. Sometimes embedded in larger worlds (WoW battlegrounds). Across genres they are called maps (FPS/RTS), tracks (racing), arenas (general). Smaller, more intimate spatial knowledge developed; competitive multiplayer requires tactical mastery of layout, hiding spots, sightlines, cover. Figure 5.2 anchors the de_dust2 B-rush worked example in Counter-Strike: Source (2004): shotgun loadout dictates close-range engagement and route choice (avoid central + right corridors that favor enemy rifles; take route B which offers cover). Movement-vs-cover discipline differs by game physics (1-shot-kill in CS:S vs multi-shot in Unreal Tournament 1999 makes constant movement more conducive to survival in UT, cover-based bursts more important in CS:S).

outline.title: From Space to Place
outline.summary: The chapter's residual-phenomenology centerpiece. Cognitive mapping nests across scales: immediate map (Counter-Strike) / level (Medal of Honor) / region (Oblivion) / world (WoW). The B-rush worked example continues (Figure 5.3) — flash-grenade response: blind D-key right-step + S+D back-wall descent, mouse-left to face up-steps anticipating counter-terrorist pursuit. As cognitive maps improve, spatial disposition shifts FROM CONCEPTUAL TO INHABITED: less conscious orientation-attention required, environment becomes part of the player's immediate surroundings (Rheric's landmark-driven WoW orientation testimony at lines 2996-3003 — visual-person, fly-pattern Undercity-Tarren-Mill, comfort and pride). Tuan 2007 (p.73) quoted as the criterion: 'When space feels thoroughly familiar to us, it has become place. Kinesthetic and perceptual experience as well as the ability to form concepts are required for the change if the space is large.' Calleja stresses the visual-aspect primacy in digital environments because heat/smell/varied-sound cues are absent or restricted. Lynch 1960 imageability quoted at length (lines 3047-3058): quality of physical objects yielding strong evokable mental images; legibility, distinctness, invitation to extended sensuous grasp; the well-oriented familiar observer. Calleja extends Lynch from physical to virtual objects, and argues imageability is EVEN MORE important in primarily visual/auditory virtual environments. The paradigm contrast: WoW Azeroth (high imageability — distinct palettes, vegetation, building styles, geographic-implausibility tolerated for distinction; Rheric on Silverpine/Barrens/Stonetalon/Arathi/Hillsbrad/Alterac palettes) vs Planetside Auraxis (lower imageability — geographically more plausible but harder to familiarize; Kestra testimony at lines 3100-3103 on continent-monotony and 'just as lost a week later'). Map ↔ 3D-environment transition (Figure 5.4 from Oblivion) as the indexical-to-inhabited shift; freeing of attention resources enables deeper involvement in other dimensions.

outline.title: The Space of Miniatures
outline.summary: Disembodied isometric spatiality, characteristic of turn-based and real-time strategy + simulation. Players are on the outside looking in; cannot be lost in miniature space (lines 3140-3142). Agency tied to a conjunction of miniature-unit capabilities and the player's disembodied-but-omniscient powers (Empire: Total War 2009 example — Portugal-marching + Silesian-tax-rate simultaneity). RTS landscape paradigm: Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War II (2009; Figure 5.5) — terrain built to support miniature interaction with defendable positions, cover, lines-of-fire calibrated to weapon ranges. Resources (mineable locations, special items, build-zones) make miniature landscapes TACTICAL spaces. Some miniature environments are purely SYMBOLIC: Risk (2009), checkers, chess — spatial involvement = spatial control = tactical involvement, inextricably coupled. The closing summary paragraph (lines 3189-3194): spatial-involvement frame defines engagement with spatial qualities of virtual environments in terms of spatial control, navigation, exploration; accounts for the internalization process that gives players the sense of inhabiting a place rather than merely perceiving a representation of space.

concepts.label: virtual-environment habitation (master metaphor)
concepts.gloss: The dimension's master concept: cumulative internalization of game-space yields the sense of INHABITING a place rather than merely PERCEIVING a representation. Anticipates IG-10's incorporation thesis.

concepts.label: exploration (macro phase)
concepts.gloss: Off-line + on-line drive to traverse unfamiliar simulated landscapes; routed through Tuan 1998's urbanization-driven romanticization of pastoral/exotic settings; differentiated from non-ergodic mental imagery by the ergodic-traversal requirement.

concepts.label: navigable space (micro phase organizing concept)
concepts.gloss: Interconnected simulated spatial cells through which the avatar moves, network organized maze-like, much of the space off-screen; accessibility depends on navigational ability. Distinguished from merely-represented space.

concepts.label: cognitive mapping (Tolman 1948 via Golledge+Garling 2004)
concepts.gloss: Encoding, storing, manipulating experienced/sensed information that can be spatially referenced; mental model accumulating spatial information into coherent internal image facilitating learning and recall. Accumulated via navigation + vantage-point/map surveying.

concepts.label: mental cartography across nested scales
concepts.gloss: Spatial internalization operates across nested scales: immediate / map / level / region / world. Counter-Strike (map), Medal of Honor (level), Oblivion (region), WoW (world).

concepts.label: imageability / legibility (Lynch 1960)
concepts.gloss: Quality of a physical object yielding strong evokable, vividly identified, powerfully structured mental images of the environment. Calleja extends from physical to virtual; argues imageability is more important in primarily visual/auditory virtual environments. WoW Azeroth (high) vs Planetside Auraxis (low).

concepts.label: landmark + wayfinding
concepts.gloss: Cognitive maps built through chains of landmarks and recognizable routes. Rheric: 'I drive by landmarks not by road names … I naturally seek certain kinds of landmarks to help me keep my bearings. A twist in the road here, a tree there.'

concepts.label: body-relative orientation (front/back/right/left, futurity-ahead)
concepts.gloss: Avatar's embodied presence retains the physical-world orientation structure: front/back/left/right with future-ahead, past-behind. Goal-directed movement reinforces the meaningfulness of these directions.

concepts.label: lost-ness as productive spatial-affect condition
concepts.gloss: Getting lost requires spatial contingency, which requires the environment to extend beyond what is immediately perceptible (Klastrup 2004 worldness). Once the player realizes loss is impossible, exploration scope collapses; the productive AFFECT of being lost is what makes exploration involving rather than mechanical.

concepts.label: place (Tuan space→place transition)
concepts.gloss: 'When space feels thoroughly familiar to us, it has become place. Kinesthetic and perceptual experience as well as the ability to form concepts are required for the change if the space is large.' The dimension's central qualitative-shift criterion.

concepts.label: vista / tourist moment (exploration-affect)
concepts.gloss: Picturesque-landscape encounter triggers tourist-mode affect: pausing on snow-capped mountain peak (Kelly 2004), wanting to take a screenshot of a great view (Rheric), 'you come over a hill and, bang, you're struck by the scenery' (Baal). Affective tonality internal to spatial macro phase.

concepts.label: transit (diegetic + non-diegetic)
concepts.gloss: Breaks in navigational flow as new zones load. Designers conceal these by channeling players through diegetically-plausible locations (Dead Space elevator). The transit moment is where rhizomatic structure becomes phenomenologically continuous.

concepts.label: 5 spatial structures (taxonomy)
concepts.gloss: Calleja's signature taxonomy: (1) unicursal corridors/labyrinths, (2) multicursal corridors/mazes, (3) rhizomatic zones, (4) open landscapes, (5) arenas. Based on TRAVERSABLE rather than visible space.

concepts.label: unicursal corridor / labyrinth
concepts.gloss: Single-path traversal with forward/backward orientation only; restrictions may be disguised (Medal of Honor: Allied Assault beach). Designer-control benefits in scripted narrative and orchestrated affect.

concepts.label: multicursal corridor / maze
concepts.gloss: Branching paths + dead ends; encourages navigational attention and mental mapping. Mental mapping required only when presented in 1st/3rd-person and extending beyond the screen. Fable (in-perspective) vs Pacman (omniscient).

concepts.label: rhizomatic zone
concepts.gloss: Non-contiguous zones linked by teleportation/loading-breaks. No-hierarchy/no-center multiplicity, multiple entry points, non-linear, resilient to local damage. Fable II + Mass Effect paradigms.

concepts.label: open landscape
concepts.gloss: Maximum navigational freedom; restrictions tend to be rule-based not spatial-structural. Oblivion, LotRO, WoW. Carries Babic's relational-space argument.

concepts.label: arena
concepts.gloss: 'Canvas for a performance.' Embedded competitive space (FPS map, racing track, RTS map). Demands intimate tactical knowledge; layout interacts with rules + player/weapon capabilities.

concepts.label: miniature space (disembodied/isometric)
concepts.gloss: Outside-looking-in spatiality of RTS/turn-based/simulation. Cannot be lost. Tactical/control involvement, not habitational. Dawn of War II (RTS), Empire: Total War, Risk (symbolic miniature).

concepts.label: tactical space (resource/control field)
concepts.gloss: Miniature landscapes designed around tactical affordances: resource locations, cover, lines-of-fire calibrated to unit speeds + weapon ranges. Internalization = exploitation of locational tactical potential.

concepts.label: embodied avatar presence (1st/3rd person)
concepts.gloss: Avatar grants the player a located orientation in the simulated environment. The condition for habitation-style spatial involvement, distinguished from miniature/disembodied.

concepts.label: absolute vs relational space (Babic 2007 via Löw 2001)
concepts.gloss: Absolute = Euclidean container, objectively-measurable arrangements (pre-MMOG game-space design). Relational = constituted by relations and interactions of actors and objects within (MMOGs through persistent social interaction). Lefebvre/Soja/Tuan as relational theorists.

concepts.label: designer-constituted contingency (Malaby 2007)
concepts.gloss: Maze contingency is CONTRIVED (correct route + dead ends designed in); uncharted bush contingency is REAL (no designed solution). Game-world design fabricates 'complex, implicit, contingent conditions wherein the texture of engaged human experience can happen.'

concepts.label: worldness (Klastrup 2004)
concepts.gloss: Defining element of virtual worlds: the structure must yield a degree of spatial contingency such that paths have surrounding environment, retaining landscape-explorability. Without worldness, exploration scope collapses.

concepts.label: cognitive-conceptual to inhabited shift
concepts.gloss: As cognitive maps improve, spatial disposition shifts from the conceptual to the inhabited. Less conscious orientation-attention required; environment becomes part of player's immediate surroundings. This is the dimension's qualitative transition.

concepts.label: attentional-resource freeing through internalization
concepts.gloss: Once spatial knowledge is internalized, attention resources free up for engagement with other PIM dimensions. The bridge to multi-dimensional incorporation (IG-10).

concepts.label: indexical-map ↔ 3D-environment transition
concepts.gloss: Making the transition from indexical map (top-down representation) to inhabited 3D environment involves a distinction between detached learning-orientation and immersed habitation. Both contribute to spatial involvement.

concepts.label: intimate map knowledge (competitive arena precondition)
concepts.gloss: Arenas develop the most intimate spatial knowledge; required for competitive play. Knowledge of hiding spots, sightlines, cover, movement-versus-space relations (CS:S knife-rush velocity).

concepts.label: goal-directed orientation reinforcement
concepts.gloss: Goal (quest / NPC-set / player-set) gives front/back/right/left renewed meaning. Reinforces avatar tangibility through directional purposefulness.

concepts.label: designer-constituted spatial-restriction-enables-other-dimensions (King+Krzywinska 2006)
concepts.gloss: Restriction of spatial freedom (labyrinth) allows tighter designer control of other involvement dimensions: scripted narrative more conveyable, orchestrated affect more reliably triggered.

positions.label: Spatial involvement is fundamentally HABITATIONAL, not merely PERCEPTUAL
positions.summary: Calleja's strongest claim: the dimension is defined by the qualitative shift from perceiving-a-representation to inhabiting-a-place, executed through cumulative cognitive-cartographic internalization. This anticipates and grounds the incorporation thesis of IG-10.

positions.label: Place emerges from space through familiarization across nested scales (Tuan-anchored)
positions.summary: Tuan 2007's space-to-place criterion is the dimension's central qualitative gatekeeper. Familiarization requires kinesthetic + perceptual experience + concept-formation. Large spaces require the most internalization work.

positions.label: Imageability is MORE important in virtual than physical environments (Lynch-extension)
positions.summary: Calleja's signature extension of Lynch: virtual environments, being primarily visual-auditory and lacking heat/smell/sound-variety cues, depend even more heavily on imageable design. Azeroth/Auraxis contrast is the empirical case.

positions.label: Calleja's 5-structure taxonomy supersedes Nitsche's labyrinth/tracks-and-rails distinction
positions.summary: Because Calleja's taxonomy is grounded in TRAVERSABLE rather than VISIBLE space, the labyrinth/tracks-and-rails distinction collapses: both structure navigable space along a single path. Methodological position against Nitsche 2008.

positions.label: Miniature space cannot host habitational spatial involvement
positions.summary: Disembodied isometric spatiality (RTS, board-game derivatives) hosts spatial CONTROL involvement but not spatial HABITATION involvement. Cannot be lost; players are always on the outside looking in. This bifurcates the dimension into habitational and tactical-control modes.

tensions.label: Space-vs-Place tension (Tuan-internal)
tensions.summary: Calleja inherits Tuan's space/place distinction but must operate it on designer-constituted environments. The familiarization criterion is preserved, but the question of whether designer-constituted place is the same KIND of place as Tuan's humanistic-geographic place is unresolved — Calleja proceeds as if it is. This is the chapter's deepest unresolved tension and the entry point for the dissertation's Umwelt augmentation.

tensions.label: Fidelity-vs-Meaningfulness tension (Auraxis case)
tensions.summary: Planetside's Auraxis is MORE geographically plausible than WoW's Azeroth, yet players report less attachment. Geographic-realistic fidelity loses to imageability + aesthetic distinctness. Calleja sides with imageability — meaningfulness trumps fidelity — but does not theoretically resolve why this should be so.

tensions.label: Designer-constituted-vs-Emergent tension (Malaby contingency)
tensions.summary: Maze contingency is contrived; uncharted-bush contingency is real. Game-world contingency lies somewhere in between — designed but multi-pathed. Calleja celebrates the designed contingency without resolving whether the productive phenomenology of being-lost (S2) genuinely transfers to contrived spaces or merely simulates the transfer.

paradigm_worked_examples: Medal of Honor: Allied Assault opening (pp.78-79): unicursal-corridor disguise + invisible-wall cognitive-map update — the canonical unicursal worked example.
Fable hill-and-rock channeling + desert-ring (pp.80-81): the canonical 1st/3rd-person multicursal-maze worked example, illustrating illusion of open world vs concealed maze structure.
Fable II teleport + Mass Effect zone-jumps (pp.81-82): paradigm rhizomatic worked-example pair distinguishing intra-region rhizome from inter-region rhizome.

Counter-Strike: Source de_dust2 B-rush (pp.83-86 + Figures 5.2/5.3): the chapter's most detailed worked example — loadout-dictated route choice + flash-grenade blind-navigation; integrates intimate-map-knowledge, cover-discipline, and weapon-physics.

WoW Azeroth vs Planetside Auraxis (pp.88-90): the imageability-contrast worked example — high-imageability/geographic-implausibility vs lower-imageability/geographic-plausibility, with Rheric and Kestra testimony anchoring the claim that meaningfulness trumps fidelity.
Oblivion map↔3D-environment transition (pp.89-90 + Figure 5.4): the indexical-to-inhabited shift worked example.
Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War II miniature landscape (p.91 + Figure 5.5): the miniature-space-as-tactical-field worked example, illustrating cover/line-of-fire/weapon-range integration.
Empire: Total War Portugal+Silesia simultaneity (p.91): the distributed-agency miniature worked example, illustrating disembodied-omniscient spatial control.

burke_pentad.rationale: The dimension is literally about the game-as-scene: the where-of-action, the constituted ground within which the agent acts. Burke's scene-act ratio (the scene contains and constrains the act) maps directly onto Calleja's spatial-structure-constrains-affordances arguments (King+Krzywinska 2006; Aarseth labyrinth) and onto the imageability ↔ engageability claim. The five-fold spatial-structures taxonomy is effectively a typology of SCENE-AS-CONSTRAINT-ON-ACT.
burke_pentad.scene_act_ratio_pairs_with: IG-04 Kinesthetic ↔ Agency (the act-aspect of the pentad)

uexkull_construct.rationale: SIGNATURE LAYER-C CHAPTER. Uexküll's Umwelt is the subjectively-constituted environment of an organism: the perceptual signs (Merkwelt) it can register and the effect-signs (Wirkwelt) through which it acts back on the world together constitute its lived environment. This maps onto Calleja's chapter with unusual fidelity: (a) the imageability apparatus (Lynch) is doing the work of Merkwelt — the environment's capacity to yield strong perceptual signs to the organism that traverses it; (b) the navigation/cognitive-mapping apparatus (Tolman + Liboriussen) is doing the work of the functional circle's perception-and-effect closure — the player builds a Merkwelt-based mental image precisely because action (effect) in the environment feeds back as perception; (c) the body-relative-orientation apparatus (Tuan 2007) is doing the work of Umwelt's organism-relativity — the avatar's front/back/right/left is precisely an Umwelt-style organism-centered spatial structure; (d) the space-to-place transition (Tuan 2007 p.73) is doing the work of Umwelt-constitution — what familiarization-yields-place describes IS the consolidation of a stable Merkwelt. The Layer-C signature claim: Umwelt is arguably MORE apt than Heideggerian In-der-Welt-sein for designer-constituted bounded environments BECAUSE Uexküll's biology-derived organism-relativity makes the designer-constituted boundedness a feature, not a bug — the game-designer-as-environment-builder constructs the Umwelt that the avatar-organism inhabits, exactly as the biologist studying a tick's Umwelt observes the bounded perceptual+effectual world the tick has been evolved to inhabit. Heideggerian In-der-Welt-sein, by contrast, presupposes a shared, public, non-constituted lifeworld that game-worlds precisely do not have.
uexkull_construct.calleja_cite_status: Calleja does NOT cite Uexküll anywhere in this chapter or this volume.
uexkull_construct.gibson_bridge_status: Calleja does NOT cite Gibson in this chapter or volume — per user directive, the Gibson-as-implicit-Uexküll-bridge framing is DROPPED. The Umwelt bridge is direct anticipatory projection, not mediated through Gibson.
uexkull_construct.merkwelt_wirkwelt_pair_status: Merkwelt maps onto Lynch imageability + cognitive-map perception side. Wirkwelt maps onto Wolf's navigable-space-via-action side. The pair-structure tracks Calleja's macro-phase (Merkwelt-dominant: exploration as perception of unfamiliar) + micro-phase (Wirkwelt-dominant: navigation as action constituting the spatial network).

ontological_grounding.rationale: Lynch's imageability is, in its conceptual content, a theory of how environments evoke vivid, identified, structured MENTAL IMAGES — i.e., a theory of designed-environment-driven phantasia. The Aristotle De Anima III.3 phantasia apparatus + Hawhee 2009 (Moving Bodies, the corpus-indexed Burke/phantasia anchor) + Papachristou (phantasia cluster) provide the upstream ontological grounding that Lynch lacks. Calleja's claim that virtual environments depend MORE heavily on imageability than physical environments is, in phantasia-terms, a claim that designer-constituted environments operate by phantasia-evocation in a way that natural environments do not.
ontological_grounding.secondary_term: Heideggerian Verlorenheit + In-der-Welt-sein (less apt than Umwelt — see Layer C signature claim above)
ontological_grounding.secondary_rationale: Calleja's lost-in-the-game-world section reads as a Heideggerian Verlorenheit analysis without the Heideggerian apparatus. But the dissertation's signature move (Layer C) is to argue that Uexküll's Umwelt is BETTER suited than Heideggerian In-der-Welt-sein for designer-constituted environments — so Heidegger is the secondary/lesser-apt ontological-grounding candidate, not the primary.
